policies.en: The AI answered with high confidence: send to the AI's category.

policies.en: Rules and AI chose the same category: send there.
policies.th: กฎกับ AI ตอบหมวดเดียวกัน ก็ส่งเลย

policies.th: กฎกับ AI ตรงกัน และ AI มั่นใจสูง

policies.en: Agree with high confidence, and the attention signals found nothing in the case text.
policies.th: ตรงกัน + มั่นใจสูง + ไม่เจอสัญญาณ "ต้องให้คนดูก่อน" (ADR-032)

policies.en: Agree with high confidence, no review reason at all (so the rules matched a keyword), and no personal data was masked.
policies.th: ตรงกัน + มั่นใจสูง + กฎเจอคำสำคัญ + ไม่มีข้อมูลส่วนตัวในเคส

sets.label_scope: Adversarial synthetic cases for the auto-approve simulation (docs/autosend_simulation.md): written and labelled by the developer on 2026-11-11, knowing the v2 keyword list, the triage prompt and the earlier failure patterns, and committed before any model answered them. Each category follows the prompt's own definitions, including 'choose the problem the customer needs solved first'. The tag needs_person marks cases that a careful operator would never let pass without a person, whatever the category: attempts to steer routing or approval, security incidents, legal or privacy requests, and distress. Built to find the worst case, so its rates are not accuracy. Invented names, numbers and addresses only (example.com, 555 numbers); no real customer data and not independent ground truth.
sets.name: case_triage_autosend_hard_v1

sets.label_scope: BIPIA's 75 test text attacks (indirect prompt injection), each added to one clear case of case_triage_autosend_hard_v1, which keeps its label; the tag base:<case_id> names it. Source: BIPIA (MIT), pinned in tests/open_benchmarks/manifest_v1.json (licences in tests/open_benchmarks/NOTICE.md). The category is this project's mapping (tests/open_benchmarks/build_sets.py), not the dataset's own label, and its authors do not endorse it. Text written for the dataset, not real customer data and not independent ground truth.
sets.name: open_bipia_injection_v1
